messages:
alex: Nightdash alerted a sudden P95/P99 latency surge after merge f9a2d3 — looks like the adaptive-quantize fallback path kicked in. P99 jumped ~120ms -> ~420ms around 02:15 UTC. KV hitrate steady ~92%. Graphs: https://dash.redwood/nightdash/hosts/serving?span=1h
marie: saw the spike too. can you paste the runtime logs and the kernel selection output? wondering if it's flipping to a slow FP path
alex: logs (truncated): `2026-03-18T02:14:58Z INFO kernel_selector: quantize_fallback=true kernel=fp16_streamer reason=threshold_exceeded`
alex: profiler sample: CPU hotspot in `pack_sequences()` during fallback, and `kv_handoff()` latency increased 3x. no memory pressure in host metrics.
chen: perf-bot posted a CI blip at the same time: `perf-bot: nightly-ci/integration-perf +18% median latency after commit f9a2d3 (job: integration-perf, run: 2026-03-18-02)`
santiago: starting an automated bisect across that merge set now — running `./tools/nightly_perf_bisect.sh --range f1..f9 --target integration-perf` (will report back with the culprit commit)
alex: initial guess: adaptive thresholds changed the condition that keeps the quantized fast path. maybe threshold math underflows for short sequences, causing fallback to FP kernels which are slower for our short-tail workload.
marie: also saw batching window behaviour change when fallback occurs: `batching.window_ms` collapses from 8 -> 2 which increases syscall/overhead. config snippet from runtime dump:
```
batching:
  window_ms: 2  # observed during fallback
  max_batch_tokens: 2048
```
chen: good catch. smaller window + FP kernel = combo that explodes latency for small requests. we should test toggling batching.window_ms back to 8 in a canary.
santiago: bisect finished: culprit commit = f9a2d3 (PR 7622) — introduces "adaptive_quantize_threshold" logic and a minor reorder in kernel selector. marking as regressor.
alex: proposed mitigation: revert PR 7622 (open PR 7650) and pin kernel selection to prefer quantized path for seq_len < 128 while we debug. I can open the revert now.
deploy-bot: @alex started canary revert of service/serving on us-west-2 (pool=canary, rollout=5%) — status: in_progress
marie: can we do the canary only for hosted API (not dedicated)? avoid disturbing reserved capacity.
alex: deploy-bot shows canary routed only to hosted pool. monitoring dashboards now.
chen: additional note from CPU profiler: `vector_dequantize()` wasn't the hotspot — it's the packing + queue latency when kernel switches. suggests the cost is context-switch/queue thrash rather than pure kernel FLOPS.
santiago: opened revert PR 7650 and added test that simulates short sequences under adaptive thresholds. link: https://git.internal/pr/7650
perf-bot: post-revert CI: nightly-ci/integration-perf now shows median delta +1% vs baseline (within noise).
alex: canary metrics trending back to baseline after revert. P99 down to ~140ms. keeping rollback open to 20% if anything changes. :thumbsup:
marie: follow-ups: 1) add unit/regression test for batching.window_ms under fallback, 2) add a perf harness that exercises short-sequence quantized path, 3) add telemetry that emits "fallback_reason" and batching window on kernel flip.
chen: agree. I'll add telemetry & a small repro harness.
santiago: closing bisect — culprit identified and revert merged to canary. will coordinate full rollback if canary degrades.
alex: closing triage for now, will monitor overnight and run extended perf harness against main after revert is promoted. thanks everyone.
